title: Queue
short: First in, first out, like a line at a counter.
what: A queue is a line. New items join at the back, and you serve items from the front, so things come out in the order they went in. In Python use collections.deque: append to join, popleft to serve.
analogy: The line at a coffee shop. Whoever arrived first gets served first, and newcomers stand at the back.

frames.label: q
frames.say: An empty queue q = deque(). Items join on the right (back) and leave on the left (front).

frames.label: q
frames.say: q.append("ann"). Ann joins the empty line, so she is both the front and the back.

frames.label: q
frames.say: Bo and Cy join behind her. The queue remembers the order they arrived.

frames.label: q
frames.say: q.popleft() serves the front: Ann, who came first. With a deque this is one step.

frames.label: q
frames.say: Dee arrives and stands at the back. Bo is at the front now.

frames.label: q
frames.say: The next popleft() serves Bo. Everyone leaves in arrival order and nobody cuts in.

when: Handle things in the order they arrived
Visit level by level, nearest first (BFS)

python:
from collections import deque

q = deque()
q.append("ann")
q.append("bo")
q.append("cy")
print(q.popleft())
q.append("dee")
print(q.popleft())
print(list(q), len(q))
print(q[0])
cost: Serve from a list with pop(0)
watch: list.pop(0) shifts every other item left. Use deque.popleft().
